item.title: Emily Ratajkowski and boyfriend Romain Gavras share passionate kiss on vacation in Rome
item.description: Emily Ratajkowski and boyfriend Romain Gavras were photographed sharing a passionate kiss while strolling through the streets of Rome, Italy.
item.content:encoded:
Emily Ratajkowski and her boyfriend showed major PDA while on vacation in Italy.

The 35-year-old model and her boyfriend, Romain Gavras, 45, were photographed sharing a passionate kiss while walking through the streets of Rome.

For the outing, Ratajkowski wore a black minidress with a plunging halter neckline, which she paired with black sunglasses, a black purse and white sneakers.

Gavras kept it casual in a pair of white baggy jeans and a green button-up shirt, which he paired with sunglasses and a white baseball cap.

SYDNEY SWEENEY, SCOOTER BRAUN PACK ON PDA DURING ROMANTIC GONDOLA RIDE IN VENICE

Other photos from their Italian getaway showed the two keeping close to each other while walking around with Gavras keeping his arm around Ratajkowski's waist.

The French filmmaker previously dated pop singers Dua Lipa and Rita Ora in 2023 and 2020 respectively.

Both Lipa and Ora have also since moved on. The "Don't Start Now" singer is now married to actor Callum Turner, while Ora married director and actor, Taika Waititi, in 2022.

Ratajkowski and Gavras first sparked romance rumors in November 2025, when they were spotted out together in New York City, and were photographed with his arm around her and kissing multiple times.

Prior to her relationship with Gavras, Ratajkowski was previously married to Sebastian Bear-McClard. During their marriage, the two welcomed their now 5-year-old son, Sylvester "Sly."

"I had rules: Never miss bedtime and basically no sleepovers. These were natural and easy to abide by," she wrote in The Cut about dating as a single mom. "There was nowhere I’d rather be than when I woke up with my toddler, so no matter the number of martinis, I’d be fully dressed and out the door to relieve the sitter and be ready for my son’s 6 a.m. 'Maamaaaa!'"

item.title: Patrick Mahomes injury recovery motivation was being able to walk before his daughter
item.description: Patrick Mahomes set an unusual ACL surgery recovery goal after his knee injury: walking before his 11-month-old daughter Golden took her first steps.
item.content:encoded:
Professional athletes are simply built differently than normal people, and sometimes that manifests itself in a serious competitive nature.

It's no secret that Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is a competitive guy, but I didn't realize just how much until a new report about his injury rehab over the offseason.

It turns out the thing that drove him to get through his recovery after knee surgery was trying to walk before his 11-month-old daughter.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

An article by The Kansas City Star's Sam McDowell talks about how Mahomes' season came to an end last December when he injured his ACL and LCL in a game against the Los Angeles Chargers.

The QB had surgery in Dallas, and after that the race was on to make sure he was back on his feet before his daughter was.

"After he returned to Kansas City later in the week, he shared with some of those closest to him a more immediate goal for his recovery," McDowell wrote. "He wanted to walk before his baby daughter, 11-month-old Golden."

Now, this is the reason (alright, one of many reasons) why Patrick Mahomes has won multiple Super Bowls, and you and I haven't.

PATRICK MAHOMES LEAPS PAST DAK PRESCOTT AS NFL'S HIGHEST-PAID QB WITH RECORD CHIEFS EXTENSION WORTH $504.75M

It's also why he has a golf course at his house, and I don't even have a putting mat... although I could order one on Amazon right now and it would be here at some point tomorrow.

To be successful on a Mahomes-ian level, you have to be ultra-competitive, to the point where you're racing your kid in a made-up "who can walk first" contest.

I bet there were moments where she stood up while holding onto the couch while he was still rocking an air cast, and he started sweating. That's how bad you have to hate losing if you want to be a successful quarterback.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

At the end of the piece, it's revealed that Mahomes did get the job done and was up and walking before his kiddo took her first steps.

Was there ever any doubt?

I'm not sure how many times I have to say it: if you're not the kind of quarterback who can outwalk a young toddler, you shouldn't be getting under center.

item.title: Trump's lawyers target what Letitia James won’t say about evidence in $450M case
item.description: Trump's lawyers accuse New York Attorney General Letitia James of concealing key Steve Cohen communications in the $450 million civil fraud case.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump’s legal representation is demanding an answer to a key question in the civil suit that almost cost him $464 million.

In a letter filed with the New York Supreme Court Thursday, Trump’s lawyers argue James failed to comply with a court order that required her to present "the preservation practices" and "its preservation efforts." 

The demand is the latest objection Trump’s attorneys have used to argue that the case, which is being reconsidered, is full of errors.

Trump’s attorneys believe James may have key evidence she hasn’t turned over — communications with Michael Cohen, a former attorney for Trump.

DELETED EMAIL DETAILS ALLEGED TRUMP-TARGETING PUSH INSIDE LETITIA JAMES’ OFFICE: ‘FIND AND PURSUE CRIMES’

"In seeking the discovery, defendants rely on a January 16, 2026 article by Cohen, published on the online platform Substack in which he asserted that, in meetings with lawyers from [James’s] office, he had ‘felt pressured and coerced to only provide information and testimony that would satisfy the government’s desire to build the cases against and secure a judgement and convictions against President Trump," a court filing says.

Cohen was a star witness in the civil suit.

During trial, he helped build the case that Trump had routinely misrepresented the value of his properties and testified that Trump had given him target net worth numbers to meet.

Although the judge denied the request for additional discovery, the process during which parties disclose relevant information about the case, he did require James to detail the process it has used to maintain and preserve information.

Trump’s attorneys maintain James failed to do so.

"[New York Attorney General’s Office] also carefully avoids representing one way or the other whether any requested materials in fact exist, and, if they do, whether NYAG has confirmed that they are being preserved," they wrote.

"Instead of actually complying with the Order, NYAG has simply recited in general terms that her ‘standard litigation hold procedures’ have been in place since the investigation phase of this matter."

The back-and-forth is the most recent development of the civil suit James brought against Trump in 2022, accusing him of habitually inflating the value of his property to a fraudulent extent.

LETITIA JAMES FACES SCRUTINY AFTER NEW YORK CITY SPENDS $81,700 PER HOMELESS PERSON AMID SHELTER SCANDALS

After being found liable, Trump was ordered to pay $355 million, plus interest, in disgorgement and was banned from applying for loans from any New York bank or financial institution for three years.

He was also banned from serving as an officer or director of any New York company for two years.

Although an appeals court later vacated the monetary penalties, James has appealed to reinstate them. Trump, for his part, has argued the case is fundamentally flawed and that it should be thrown out in its entirety.

Earlier this month, Trump’s lawyers cited five key disqualifying weaknesses.

They argue that Attorney General James lacked the authority to bring the case, noting that the case involves private commercial transactions rather than harm to the public. They also contend that Trump’s valuations reflected subjective estimates that lenders independently evaluated rather than fraudulent misrepresentations.

"The only supposed 'victims' here are a handful of ultrasophisticated banks and insurers that have never claimed to be injured, were eager to do business with President Trump and his family, and made over $100 million from these transactions," the appeal states.

They further argue that the prosecution’s premise of overvaluation is based on the misguided idea that real estate has one objective value, and that deviations from that value must be fraud.

"Under that breathtakingly broad theory, NYAG can second-guess any business transaction in this State on almost any imagined grounds," attorneys wrote.

On the penalties, Trump’s lawyers argue the $450 million disgorgement is excessive, unlawful and even unconstitutional.

Finally, the appeal argues that the politically charged nature of the case, on its own, should have been enough to halt its consideration.

"NYAG cannot point to a single Section 63(12) enforcement action against similarly situated developers (or any other type of defendant) based on practices comparable to those alleged here," the filing states, referring to the state law Trump was accused of violating.

On the matter of its disclosures, James’ office pointed to its own letter in response to an inquiry from Fox News Digital, contending that it had met its disclosure requirements.

TRUMP BACKS REPUBLICAN CHALLENGER TO OUST LETITIA JAMES AMID ONGOING MORTGAGE FRAUD FEUD

"Insofar as Defendants have sought or are seeking more information about OAG’s specific preservation efforts, OAG objects to the demand for this extrajudicial discovery," the letter states.

"Moreover, OAG has completely satisfied its obligations under the Court’s Order for OAG to identify the preservation practices that existed and applied and continue to exist and apply."

item.title: Former Cal softball player files lawsuit against university, female ex-coach over alleged sexual misconduct
item.description: Chelsea Spencer allegedly pressured a Cal softball player into a sexual relationship and cut her playing time, according to a new lawsuit filed in court.
item.content:encoded:
A former University of California, Berkeley softball player is accusing an ex-head coach of using her position of authority to pressure the player into a sexual relationship and allegedly threatening her playing time if she ended it.

The complaint, filed Aug. 24 in Alameda County Superior Court and obtained by OutKick, alleges Cal failed to intervene and allowed Chelsea Spencer to remain as head coach for months after athletic department staff learned of the alleged relationship.

Spencer ultimately stepped down last year in June, four months after agreeing to a multi-year contract extension. According to the lawsuit, a subsequent Cal investigation concluded that Spencer had violated campus policy regarding conflicts of interest in consensual relationships. The filing does not detail the dates when the probe started or ended. It also alleged Spencer was not cooperative in the process.

SJSU VOLLEYBALL COACH'S ALLEGED ASSAULT VICTIM SPEAKS OUT FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE ALLEGATIONS SURFACED

In an email to OutKick on Friday, a Cal spokesperson declined to comment on the lawsuit or the school's investigation into Spencer.

The former softball player retained the services of Slater Slater Schulman law firm. Gizem Gures, an attorney at the firm, referenced Cal’s reputation and its response to the investigation in a statement to USA Today Sports about the lawsuit.

"Berkeley proudly holds itself out as the No. 1 public university in the world. That reputation comes with a responsibility to protect its students. As a Cal alum, it is deeply disappointing to see what our client experienced and how the University responded after its own investigation substantiated the conduct. Our client deserved better. Berkeley's students deserve better. The University needs to do better," the statement read.

The complaint further alleges that Spencer’s advances toward the former player started in fall 2023, after the unnamed player joined the softball team as an incoming transfer. It says Spencer contacted her daily, via phone calls and text messages. Those communications eventually took on a romantic tone.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

At one point, Spencer allegedly told the player, "you’re so beautiful" and "your girlfriend is so lucky." The complaint further alleges that Spencer shared details about her personal life and gave gifts in the form of cash.

Once the player effectively ignored the coach's messages, Spencer allegedly became angry and cut her playing time as punishment, the complaint claims.

"When Plaintiff did not provide Spencer the attention she demanded, Spencer yelled at Plaintiff, treated her differently, and reduced or withheld Plaintiff's playing opportunities," the complaint states. "Plaintiff thus began to recognize, even before the relationship became sexual, that Spencer's personal demands and Spencer's authority as Head Coach were intertwined."

The former player argued that Spencer’s conduct and the university’s alleged negligence caused her severe emotional distress and forced her to end her collegiate softball career earlier than she would have otherwise. She is seeking a jury trial and damages for personal injuries and other losses.

item.title: ICE officer pleads not guilty to lying about Minneapolis shooting involving Venezuelan man
item.description: Video evidence allegedly contradicted the ICE officer's claims about the Minneapolis shooting of Venezuelan man Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, prosecutors say.
item.content:encoded:
A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer pleaded not guilty Friday to charges of lying about a January shooting of a Venezuelan man in Minneapolis during the Trump administration's crackdown on illegal immigration.

Christian Castro appeared in a Texas federal court where he faces six charges of making "materially false" statements to investigators, according to federal court documents unsealed Friday. He turned himself in to authorities Thursday evening.

A judge ordered Castro released on a $75,000 unsecured bond and required him to wear an ankle monitor.

DOJ CHARGES ICE OFFICER WITH LYING TO INVESTIGATORS FOLLOWING MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING OF VENEZUELAN MAN

The charges stem from the Jan. 14 shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, a Venezuelan man who was shot in the leg. Moments earlier, Castro and his partner attempted to stop a vehicle.

The driver, also a Venezuelan citizen, fled, triggering a foot chase.

Castro caught up to the driver and a physical struggle ensued, according to the indictment. Sosa-Celis attempted to help the driver, and they both fled into a nearby apartment duplex and shut the door.

ICE AGENTS IN FATAL HOUSTON SHOOTING WERE NOT WEARING BODY CAMERAS, SOURCES SAY

Castro drew his service weapon and fired a single shot through the front door, striking Sosa-Celis in the leg, federal prosecutors said.

Two 1-year-old children and two women were inside the home when Castro opened fire, prosecutors added.

In an attempt to justify the shooting, Castro allegedly told investigators he was brutally assaulted by multiple individuals wielding tools, claiming he was hit with a broom and a snow shovel during the confrontation. He also claimed he was on his back when he fired toward the fleeing men, officials said.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS LOST OR ABANDONED HUNDREDS OF LAWSUITS AGAINST ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS, MIGRANTS: REPORT

However, video evidence later contradicted those statements, prompting an investigation. Federal prosecutors said Castro was standing up when he opened fire, and they disputed his claim that he fought the suspect on the ground for three minutes, noting the struggle actually lasted about 11 seconds.

The shooting occurred amid a targeted crackdown on illegal immigration in Minneapolis.

Castro faces separate charges in Minnesota and was previously arrested in Texas in May.

ICE OFFICER CHARGED IN MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING RELEASED IN TEXAS AFTER JUDGE DECLINES TO INTERVENE

His case has sparked a legal battle involving Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, who has refused to extradite him to Minnesota.

item.title: Robot dog could deliver your next package and an ad
item.description: Robot.com's R-dog uses articulated legs and wheels to climb stairs and deliver packages, while its built-in screens display paid ads along the route.
item.content:encoded:
We've covered robot dogs patrolling with police and training to handle terrain that could someday take them to the moon. We've even watched wheeled versions tackle some pretty wild ground. And whenever we show these machines, one question keeps coming up: What happens when they reach a flight of stairs? Well, Robot.com may have an answer.

Its new four-legged R-dog is built to carry packages where traditional wheeled delivery robots can get stuck. It can also show ads along the way, turning your future delivery into something of a moving billboard.

So, can R-dog really get your package closer to your front door while making the economics of robot delivery work? Let's take a closer look.

ONE-WHEELED AI SECURITY ROBOT COULD PATROL YOUR PROPERTY

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

R-dog is Robot.com's latest concept for autonomous delivery. The San Francisco-based company unveiled it on Aug. 11. The idea tackles one of the most frustrating parts of robotic delivery: the final stretch to your door. A wheeled robot may handle the sidewalk just fine, only to meet a curb or staircase it cannot cross. Robot.com designed R-dog to cover those final 330 feet with a mix of wheels and articulated legs.

Each leg ends in a wheel, so R-dog can roll efficiently across flatter ground. When the route gets more difficult, those flexible legs are designed to help it deal with stairs, curbs and other obstacles. The cargo compartment forms most of the robot's body. Robot.com says it can carry food orders and standard packages inside.

And yes, it definitely looks like a robot dog. There is even a tail, which gives the machine a friendlier appearance than your average delivery box on wheels. That personality may be more than decoration. Robot.com wants people to notice R-dog, interact with it and feel comfortable when it appears in public spaces. As you will see, that becomes especially important once advertising enters the picture.

Getting a delivery robot across town can actually be easier than getting it from the sidewalk to your front door. Traditional delivery robots tend to perform best on predictable surfaces. Smooth sidewalks work well because wheels are efficient and relatively simple.

Then the terrain changes. A staircase can end the trip. A high curb can cause trouble. Even an awkward building entrance may force someone to step in. That creates an obvious weak point in a system that is supposed to reduce human involvement. Robot.com wants R-dog to keep going when a standard sidewalk robot would have to stop.

Its four-legged design could also expand the places where autonomous delivery makes sense. Campuses, apartment complexes and neighborhoods can all include routes that become difficult for wheels alone. Of course, getting over the obstacle is only useful if the package also reaches the right person. That brings us to R-dog's unusual delivery system.

The cargo compartment can hold multiple items, including stacked food orders and e-commerce packages. Once R-dog reaches its destination, an unattended auto drop-off system releases the order. The robot can then continue to its next assignment. And yes, the visual is hard to ignore.

The package appears to slide out through the back of the robot. There really is no delicate way to say this: It looks a little like R-dog poops out your delivery. Funny visual aside, the system could have a practical advantage. You would not necessarily need to stand outside and physically unload the robot before it could leave.

Still, one question remains. Robot.com says the compartment can carry multiple orders, but its current materials do not explain exactly how the concept chooses the correct package when several items are loaded inside. That is one of the details I want to see explained as R-dog gets closer to real-world deployment. The company is still refining parts of the prototype, including its storage setup.

HUMANOID ROBOTS WORK NONSTOP IN PACKAGE TEST

Now we get to the part that makes R-dog more than a quirky delivery machine. The robot has two video screens connected to R-ads, Robot.com's advertising platform. Brands can remotely manage campaigns shown on the company's robots.

In other words, every trip can potentially earn money twice. The robot can perform a delivery while its screens carry paid advertising through the neighborhood. That business model makes some sense. People already ignore plenty of static advertising. A four-legged robot rolling past with a tail has a much better chance of making someone look.

You might stop to watch it. Maybe you pull out your phone for a photo or video. Someone else could share that clip on social media. From an advertiser's perspective, that kind of attention can be valuable. Robot.com also promotes natural voice conversations, allowing R-dog to respond when people interact with it. That could make the advertising experience more engaging than simply walking past another screen.

The company says R-ads also offer campaign analytics. However, its public R-dog materials leave some details about those measurements unclear. I would like to know exactly what the system measures when people interact with these robots and how that information gets handled. Those answers become more important if machines like R-dog eventually appear in busy public spaces.

Of course, legs alone do not get a robot safely through a crowded neighborhood. It also needs to understand what is happening around it. Robot.com is working with FieldAI on the navigation stack planned for the production version of R-dog.

FieldAI's Field Foundation Models are designed to help robots operate in changing real-world environments without requiring prior mapping. That could allow R-dog to adapt when the route ahead looks different from what it expected, whether someone left an object in the way or the path suddenly changes.

Robot.com also runs its fleet through a platform called REMI. The company describes REMI as its fleet-management platform and physical API layer. The advantage here is that R-dog does not need an entirely separate operational system. Robot.com can plug the new four-legged design into technology it already uses across its fleet.

CEO and co-founder Felipe Chavez Cortes summed up that strategy when he said, "We built R-dog to run on what already exists."

Robot.com already has robots in the real world

R-dog may be new, but Robot.com has already spent years putting robots to work. The company was founded in 2017 and is headquartered in San Francisco, with additional offices in Colombia. Robot.com says more than 500 robots are deployed across the United States and Canada, plus Dubai and other MENA markets. Those machines have completed more than 2.5 million tasks.

Its lineup includes R-kiwi for sidewalk delivery and R-cargo for industrial logistics. Robot.com also develops R-noid, a humanoid platform aimed at workplace tasks. That existing fleet gives Robot.com experience to build on.

Robot.com says commercial deployments are targeted for 2027. The company's CEO has said college campuses will come first, although Robot.com has yet to announce specific campuses or cities. That makes campuses a logical proving ground. They offer lots of short deliveries, plenty of foot traffic and exactly the kinds of curbs or stairways that R-dog was designed to handle.

Robot.com already operates campus delivery robots in North America and expanded its autonomous delivery partnership with Sodexo in August 2026.

Pricing has not been announced. And do not expect to walk into a store and buy an R-dog for your house. At least initially, Robot.com appears focused on commercial delivery pilots and brand activations rather than individual consumers.

For now, businesses can sign up for early access to delivery pilots and advertising activations ahead of the planned 2027 rollout.

NEW WHEELED ROBOT SAYS NO THANKS TO HUMANOID HYPE

If R-dog performs the way Robot.com hopes, robot delivery could get closer to your actual doorstep instead of stopping at the sidewalk. That could make autonomous delivery practical in more places and reduce the number of times a person has to step in to finish the trip.

But R-dog also gives us a preview of where the economics of robot delivery may be heading. Moving a package is one revenue opportunity. Selling advertising during the journey creates another. That means your future delivery experience could look very different. The same machine bringing dinner to your door might also be displaying a commercial as it rolls away.

Convenience will get plenty of attention, but I will also be watching the privacy side. Robot.com should be clear about what its advertising system measures when people approach or interact with R-dog.

I have seen plenty of robot dogs that can climb, jump or show off in a demo. R-dog caught my attention because Robot.com is trying to apply those abilities to a very ordinary problem: getting a package all the way to your door. Wheels are great until the sidewalk ends. 

Giving a delivery robot articulated legs could help it complete routes that stop other machines short. The advertising angle may be equally important to whether this idea works as a business. If R-dog can earn money from an ad while it is already out making a delivery, that gives operators another reason to deploy it. 

Still, R-dog remains a concept heading toward commercial use in 2027. I want to see how it handles real stairs, crowded sidewalks and everyday weather before calling the problem solved. I also want more details about how multiple packages get sorted during unattended deliveries and what information R-ads collect from public interactions. Those answers will tell us a lot about whether R-dog becomes a useful delivery tool or simply a very clever way to get people to look at a screen.

Would you be comfortable with a robot dog climbing your steps to deliver a package if it was also showing ads along the way, or would you rather stick with a human at the door? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Legendary sports agent talks about the Rams use of 'caponomics' to bring Aaron Donald out of retirement
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams used void years, backloaded contracts, and creative cap moves to fit Aaron Donald's $20 million deal alongside Myles Garrett and more.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Donald officially made his return to the Los Angeles Rams earlier this week. But how did a team with so many expensive contracts fit Donald under the salary cap?

According to famed sports agent Leigh Steinberg, it's because the Rams do a great job with "caponomics."

The Rams did it by "creating cap room, redoing someone else's contract so that there's less salary involved and by giving that player a bonus," Steinberg told OutKick in a recent interview. "If a team is creative, they can move other contracts around and create cap space."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

After falling short against their NFC West rival, the Seattle Seahawks, in the NFC Championship Game last season, the Rams went on a spending spree this offseason.

They gave MVP-winning quarterback Matthew Stafford a one-year, $55 million contract extension, traded for Kansas City Chiefs star cornerback Trent McDuffie and signed him to a four-year, $124 million contract extension, signed cornerback Jaylen Watson to a three-year, $51 million contract, and acquired Cleveland Browns superstar Myles Garrett before signing him to a five-year, $208 million contract after redoing his deal following the trade.

Despite handing out all of those massive deals, the Rams were still able to sign Donald to a one-year, $20 million deal, despite being up against the salary cap.

So how, exactly, are the Rams making it work? Exactly as Steinberg said: by being creative.

For Stafford’s deal, the Rams have pushed his contract further into the future, spreading out the cap hit using void years, meaning Stafford’s contract will count against the salary cap in even though he won’t be on the team. Stafford’s contract is spread out through the 2031 season.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

As for McDuffie, the Rams backloaded his contract. This season, McDuffie’s cap hit is just $10.8 million, but that rises to $30.8 million next season and will hover around that figure for ensuing three seasons.

Garrett’s contract is structured similarly to both Stafford’s and McDuffie’s, with a lower cap hit in the first year and larger hits later in the deal while also using void years. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year’s contract runs through 2030, but his cap hits are spread through 2034.

Here are his cap hits each year through 2034: $8.4 million, $15 million, $27.57 million, $39.875 million, $48.17 million, $17.523 million, $11.5 million, $7.6 million and finally $3.3 million.

To fit Aaron Donald into their group of superstars, the Rams have pushed a lot of money into the future to make it work in the present.

Steinberg thinks the decision to acquire Garrett and bring Donald out of retirement will be well worth it.

"So let's imagine that you took a team that was already the favorite to win the Super Bowl because of their (trade) of the best defensive player in football, Myles Garrett. And you now add to him an unbelievably dominant defensive player in Aaron Donald," Steinberg said.

PRO FOOTBALL HALL OF FAME MAKING MASSIVE OVERHAUL OF ITS SELECTION PROCESS FOLLOWING 2026 BILL BELICHICK SNUB

"It creates an impregnable line that's impossible to double team. The synergistic effect of this is that an opposing offense can't double team both Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. So somewhere in there you're going to have this spectacularly dominant player on the loose."

Steinberg is also certain that Donald, who made the Pro Bowl in each of his 10 seasons in the NFL, would not have returned unless he felt he could play at an elite level.

"I am sure that Aaron Donald would not have come back except that he thought he could be dominant once again," Steinberg said. "I'm assuming that time takes its toll. Being outside of football takes its toll, but it won't take too long for Aaron Donald to be back in form. No other team has two players like this backed up by another three."

In addition to having Donald and Garrett, the Rams’ defensive line was already strong with Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske, Byron Young and Poona Ford. Steinberg said the Rams’ defensive line could be one of the best of all time, comparing it to the legendary line the Baltimore Colts had in the 1960s.

"I think the only thing that would be equivalent was the Fearsome Foursome that had Merlin Olsen and Deacon Jones and Rosie Greer. The Fearsome Foursome is back and as you said, they've got Poona Ford and Kobie Turner and Braden Fiske and Byron Young and they're loaded with gifted players," Steinberg said.

CAM SKATTEBO CONSIDERED RETIREMENT AFTER SEASON-ENDING ANKLE INJURY IN GIANTS ROOKIE YEAR

"The Rams do a better job of scouting players, drafting players, and then finding that one superstar that can be plugged into an already dominating defense or offense."

A front comparable to the Fearsome Foursome of Olsen, Jones, Greer and Lamar Lundy would give the Rams an excellent chance of getting to the Super Bowl and winning it all.

Steinberg, who was inducted into the California Sports Hall of Fame in 2017, has had many high-profile clients. Across football and baseball, Steinberg’s clients include Steve Bartkowski, Steve Young, Troy Aikman, Warren Moon, Bruce Smith, Thurman Thomas, Kordell Stewart, Jeff George, Ben Roethlisberger, Myron Rolle, Matt Leinart, Mark Brunell, Ricky Williams, Howie Long, Eric Karros and Dusty Baker, among others.

Steinberg was not surprised that Donald came out of retirement because so many of his clients wanted to as well.

"I had 64 first-round draft picks, 12 of the players in the Hall of Fame, and when they retired, they did it with class and dignity. But then a couple weeks later, the phone would ring and the player would say, ‘Do you think there's any spot for me? Do you think I can come back?’" Steinberg said.

The legendary agent said these were players who had peaceful second careers lined up and had all the money they would need, but that they simply missed the game.

"They all want to play and when they're away from the game, players miss the structure, the fact that it gives them an itinerary that tells them what they're supposed to be doing every day, what they're supposed to be doing at this time of year. They have structure. They miss the camaraderie in the locker room with the band of brothers that are around them," Steinberg said.

"They miss the electric excitement of performing in front of packed crowds and or many of them from Pop Warner on this is all they've known and so, like the moth to the flame, professional sports is so intoxicating that players never really want to retire."

The Rams are certainly fortunate that Donald wanted to come back and play. The result could end with him holding another Lombardi Trophy.

item.title: Ohio State pays $2.1M settlement as it admits researcher had ‘inappropriate foreign affiliations’ to China
item.description: Ohio State University paid $2.1 million to resolve allegations it failed to disclose researcher C.K. Shum's ties to China's Thousand Talents Program.
item.content:encoded:
The Ohio State University acknowledged that a former researcher had "inappropriate foreign affiliations" after agreeing to pay $2.1 million to resolve federal allegations that the university failed to share researchers’ ties to China while seeking and receiving taxpayer-funded research grants.

The Justice Department alleged Ohio State failed to properly disclose affiliations and financial support involving Chinese universities and state-run research organizations in applications and reports submitted to NASA and the National Science Foundation from 2012 to 2023. 

The allegations included a principal investigator’s participation in China’s Thousand Talents Program.

Ohio State told Fox News Digital in a statement Friday that the university ultimately uncovered and investigated C.K. Shum’s foreign affiliations itself and reported them to federal authorities. Shum is no longer employed at the university.

HARVARD-CHINA LINKS UNEARTHED AS CONGRESS FINDS 140 PAPERS CO-AUTHORED BY CCP MILITARY UNIVERSITIES

"Ohio State uncovered and investigated C.K. Shum’s inappropriate foreign affiliations and self-reported them to NASA and the National Science Foundation," Benjamin Johnson, chief communications officer at The Ohio State University, told Fox News Digital in a statement Friday. 

"The university suspended Shum’s principal investigator privileges, halted spending on the relevant federal awards, initiated disciplinary proceedings and repaid the federal grant funds in question. Shum is no longer employed at Ohio State, and the university has cooperated with federal authorities throughout the investigation.

"Ohio State takes national security seriously, and the university has long been recognized for its efforts to promote research integrity and security. Safeguards include dedicated research compliance and secure research offices, mandatory conflict-of-interest and research security disclosure systems and robust security and foreign influence training programs."

HARVARD TOPS NATION IN FOREIGN CASH HAUL AS COTTON DEMANDS PROBE INTO CHINA FUNDING

In a press release, the Department of Justice said the grant applications required OSU to share any ties to any foreign government.

"The settlement resolves allegations that OSU failed to disclose the collaboration and affiliation with, or funding received from, the PRC by certain OSU employees working on NASA and NSF grants," the press release said. 

"Specifically, the settlement resolves allegations that, since 2014, annual Faculty Activity Reports submitted to OSU identified affiliations with PRC universities and state-run research organizations, but OSU did not disclose this information to NASA or NSF."

The press release also noted that Ohio State became aware in 2019 that a researcher tied to NASA-funded work was involved in China’s Thousand Talents Program but waited until 2023 to inform NASA and the National Science Foundation.

The federal government describes the program as a Beijing-backed effort to attract people with expertise in or access to overseas technology and intellectual property. The DOJ also said it found other OSU employees connected to the grants who had relationships with Chinese entities or received Chinese funding.

WATCHDOG REPORT ALLEGES RED-STATE UNIVERSITY TRAINED EXECUTIVES TIED TO CHINA'S DEFENSE SECTOR

"American universities that benefit from the federal government’s support for scientific research and advancement must fully disclose all foreign funding in their grant applications," Brett Shumate, assistant attorney general of the Justice Department's Civil Division, said in a statement. 

"We will continue to hold accountable any university that fails to comply with disclosure requirements designed to protect research security and federally-funded scientific achievements."

Fox News Digital reached out to the DOJ for comment.

item.title: Illinois mother charged with murder in death of 2-year-old son in case drawing comparions to Lindsay Clancy
item.description: Corie Walsh faces three murder charges in her 2-year-old son's death, a Frankfort, Illinois, case that a neighbor says mirrors the Lindsay Clancy trial.
item.content:encoded:
An Illinois woman has been charged with three counts of murder in the death of her 2-year-old son in a case that has already drawn comparisons to the Lindsay Clancy trial, authorities confirmed.

Corie A. Walsh, 40, was being held for medical treatment on Friday after she was found with wounds believed to be self-inflicted but non-life-threatening when police responded to her home Tuesday, the Frankfort Police Department said in a news release.

Frankfort is about 36 miles southwest of Chicago.

SOCIAL MEDIA IS LINDSAY CLANCY WILD CARD THAT COULD TILT POTENTIAL RETRIAL TO THE DEFENSE, RETIRED JUDGE SAYS

Once she’s released from treatment, she will be transferred to the Will County Adult Detention Facility to await a hearing.

Frankfort police officers responded to Walsh’s home Tuesday afternoon and found her son unresponsive. He was given CPR and transported to a hospital where he was later pronounced dead.

NORTH DAKOTA MOM STABS HER 2 CHILDREN TO DEATH IN 'HORRIFIC' KILLING THAT LEFT COPS TRAUMATIZED: OFFICIALS

"Our thoughts and prayers are with the family, their loved ones and everyone affected by this heartbreaking tragedy," Frankfort police said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital. "We ask our community to keep them in their thoughts and prayers and to respect their privacy as they navigate this profoundly difficult time."

The boy was strangled, according to FOX 32.

LINDSAY CLANCY’S FUTURE COULD REST WITH ‘PROSECUTION DOCTORS’ AS CASE ECHOES INFAMOUS MAINE KILLINGS: EXPERT

Carolyn Pappas, who lives nearby, told NBC Chicago earlier this week that the boy’s death has left residents stunned. She told the station that the circumstances brought to mind the case of Clancy, a Massachusetts mother who admitted to killing her three children before attempting to take her own life.

"This is just absolutely devastating, that this could be another Lindsay Clancy situation in our neighborhood, in our community. You never think it's going to hit so close to home," she told the station. "And, so, yeah, that absolutely makes us think of that. And, again, just more people, I think, are struggling than we realize, and, so, we just need to be there for one another."

Three other people who were unharmed were found inside the Walsh home on Tuesday, police said, according to FOX 32.

Fox News' Greg Wehner contributed to this report.

item.title: Spicy Sophie Cunningham loves our vets and football season, 380-pound high school TANK & sad Rutgers fireworks
item.description: Sophie Cunningham kicks off college football season with Mizzou pride while Colorado celebrates its upset win over Georgia Tech in opening night chaos.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

I know all eyes are on the Commonwealth today (sickening, by the way), but let's all just take a step back for a second and enjoy the simpler things in life.

We're here. An actual college football Friday. Labor Day weekend. One of the most underrated weekends of the entire calendar year.

WEEK ONE UPSET SPECIAL: THESE THREE COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS SHOULD BE ON UPSET ALERT THIS WEEKEND

Football last night. Football tonight. And tomorrow. And the next day. And the day AFTER that! But wait, there's more!

After Monday, we take a full 48 hours off before the NFL season kicks off on Wednesday.

Lordy. She's here, and she's just as beautiful as I imagined. How lucky are we? What a blessing.

Let's roll.

Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham supports the vets like a patriot, and then gets us fired up for football season ... again, like a patriot.

What else? I've got a poor woman getting trucked on the sidelines in Piscataway last night, an absolute UNIT in the high school football ranks, and the Buffaloes were FEELING it after upsetting Georgia Tech.

What a scene!

OK, grab you whatever you'd like on this first Friday of September — dealer's choice today! — and settle in for a Friday 'Cap!

There she is — your Week 1 viewing schedule. It's perfect.

Honestly, though? Not the greatest Week 1 the sport has given us. LSU-Clemson is obviously the headliner tomorrow, but there's not a ton of great games before it.

The early games are a slog (except for North Texas-Indiana on FOX, of course!). The 3:30 hour gives us Baylor-Auburn and Boise State-Oregon, for those pining for the old SEC on CBS theme song.

CLEMSON'S DABO SWINNEY THROWS SHADE AT LANE KIFFIN, LSU OVER BRINGING IN NFL PLAYERS: 'IT'S EMBARRASSING'

Not a ton of competition for LSU-Clemson in the late hour. I don't care, though. It's back. We're back. Thank God.

No more WNBA talk ...

... Unless, of course, it involves Sophie Cunningham!

She leads us off today.

"Spicy Sophie tapping in."

She just refuses to miss. Let's put Sophie in the juror pool up in the Commonwealth and see how things play out!

"It's the start of a new football season. We are hyped. We're excited. We're about to kick some butt this year. Come out, be loud, and show your Mizzou pride."

Sophie gets it. She's just as tired as we are from all the WNBA nonsense. She's ready to get this season started.

PS: Sophie welcomed veterans to Gainbridge Fieldhouse all season? Lordy. Absolute patriot. Between that and the return of college football, the left is in shambles today.

OK, let's keep this class moving right along. It's a Football Friday, after all.

Anyone catch the end of the Colorado-Ga. Tech game last night? I'm not talking about the blocked field goal.

I'm talking about what happened after the blocked field goal:

Look at those maniacs! Big win, and they let the Georgia Tech student section HAVE it. Look at the one player who actually attempts to jump into the stands.

Risky little move. He got swatted away like a bug. Probably for the best. I've seen that movie end poorly far too many times.

Speaking of last night's appetizer, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into our first BIG weekend of the year.

First up? Let's go ahead and check in with the fans up in New Jersey!

Incredible. What a game for the UMass Minutemen! First win over an FBS team since 2023! Do you know how much Rutgers paid for that shellacking?

$1.5 million. It was the second largest paycheck for a LOSS in college football history:

Goodness gracious. The accounts in Piscataway are pulling their hair out today. Just a stunning upset.

That wasn't even my favorite part of the game. Anyone here stick around for the postgame fireworks?!

Amazing. The obvious question is, why not just cancel the show? I don't know. Can you do that? Can you just cancel a fireworks show because the home team lost? I assume you can just roll them over to the next home game, right?

Yikes. Never mind. USC comes to town next. I don't see that first home 'dub coming until Howard the following week.

Put those fireworks on ice, fellas!

Next? Let's get to some reader mail on the way out. I have a loaded mailbox and it needs a good Labor Day cleaning before we start the fall season.

Yesterday, we all mocked Ryan Reynolds for his absolutely baffling comments on how tough the 1980s were to live through ... because of the Cuban Missile Crisis (which ended in the '60s).

I asked y'all if there was any truth to it.

From Jeff D:

As a kid in the 80s , I can’t say that the Cuban Missile Crisis was anywhere at the top of our minds. I do remember a couple of events that were at the top of our minds — the Challenger explosion and baby Jessica being rescued from a well.

Baby Jessica was a crazy story of a little girl falling down a well and eventually being rescued, the event really brought the country together and her rescue was a joyous moment for the country.

All in all, most memories from that period were positive and I’m pretty sure the Cuban Missile Crisis never crossed our minds.

Thanks, Jeff! Would you look at that? A child was in peril in the 1980s and the entire country rallied around her. Weird. Surely that would happen in today's world, right?

... Right?

Next? From Brian S:

Ryan Reynolds went a bit overboard with the hyperbole, but it wasn’t all fun and games in the 80’s. We 80’s kids lived under the cloud of potential nuclear war for much of the decade. There was a TV movie in 1983 called "The Day After" that terrified the nation. Truly.

I think that nuclear war "threat" fed into our, "F–k it, let’s just enjoy ourselves and have a great time" attitude. There was no Cuban Missile Crisis hangover. Vietnam though? Hell yes. Just look at all the movies about that war released during the 80’s.

Now, having said all that, I’d give anything to go back there. You often write, "What a time to be alive." Well the 80’s truly embodied that.

Thanks, Brian! I may have to look up "The Day After" this weekend. Those things always fascinate me.

Finally ... From Eric P:

The 80’s was one of the best decades in history. The best music; Cars still had a little style and nothing woke about sports. Oh, and I managed to hit a 3-pointer to win a game at the buzzer over Mark Langston in an alumni game at my college against a team of Mariners.

This Reynolds idiot was 8-9 years old and there was no strife. Won’t watch his piece of s–t movie on general principles.

Thanks, Eric! I do love the cars from the '80s. One of these day, I want an old 1980s pickup truck. It's a weird dream of mine. Just to drive around town.

One of these days.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

OK, that's it for today — and this week! It's a High School Football Friday, so let's end class with an absolute UNIT out of Alabama.

See y'all Monday.

Fine. Anymore '80s nostalgia? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

item.title: Fonda rushes to defend Mark Ruffalo against antisemitism accusation, says Larry Ellison 'should be ashamed'
item.description: Jane Fonda called out Larry Ellison by name for accusing Mark Ruffalo of antisemitism, saying he should be ashamed of the tactic used in the merger fight.
item.content:encoded:
Actress and activist Jane Fonda rushed to defend actor Mark Ruffalo on Thursday after Paramount accused him of invoking antisemitic tropes, calling out Larry Ellison specifically.

"Larry Ellison, because he doesn’t like Mark Ruffalo’s position on the merger, accuses him of antisemitism when he said nothing that isn’t within his constitutional right to say. It’s a tactic they’re using. He should be ashamed of himself, Larry Ellison. But there’s a lot of support for Mark. A lot of people came forward," Fonda said in an interview at Diane von Furstenberg's DVF Awards, according to The Hollywood Reporter.

Paramount did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

JOHN CUSACK STANDS IN 'SOLIDARITY' WITH MARK RUFFALO AMID PARAMOUNT'S ANTISEMITISM ALLEGATION

Ruffalo was previously accused of invoking "antisemitic tropes" by Paramount after the Marvel star shared a video from August of Safra Catz, an Oracle executive vice chair and Paramount board member, discussing technology Oracle used to assist Israel after the Oct. 7 Hamas terrorist attacks.

The actor linked Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, the father of Paramount CEO David Ellison, to financing behind the proposed acquisition and suggested the merger would be used to push "oppression."

RABBINIC GROUP ACCUSES JEWISH ENTERTAINERS OF 'WHITEWASHING ANTISEMITISM' IN MARK RUFFALO DEFENSE

"These ‘really profoundly scary technologies’ will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day used on you," Ruffalo said. "Look how she revels in what we now have come to see as a genocide, which was built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle."

Ruffalo previously told Fox News Digital in a statement that Paramount's accusation was appalling.

PARAMOUNT ESCALATES THREAT TO LEAVE CALIFORNIA AS DEM AG'S ANTITRUST LAWSUIT STALLS WARNER BROS MERGER

"The accusation that I am antisemitic is appalling and fundamentally dishonest. Criticizing the actions of the Israeli prime minister, a military technology contract or the executives who supply it is not the same as criticizing Jewish people. This critical and necessary dialogue is then dishonestly framed as being anti-Israel," he said. "To be clear, my views come from my own political convictions and should never be interpreted as hostility toward Jewish people, for whom I have deep love and respect. Everything I know about acting, activism and humanism has been profoundly shaped by the Jewish friends, colleagues and loved ones who have been integral and family throughout every point of my life."

More than 180 Jewish entertainers and artists signed a letter Tuesday "proudly" voicing support for actor Ruffalo after he was accused of antisemitism in his opposition to the proposed Warner Bros. Discovery-Paramount merger.

"We are Jewish artists, writers, creative professionals, faith leaders and thinkers who have, in response to the outrageous smear campaign against our respected colleague Mark Ruffalo, a simple message to share with the world: Enough!" the letter read, according to Variety.

"Enough with the false and dangerous weaponization of charges of antisemitism against those who are brave enough to point out the obvious: that the assault on the Palestinian people and the assault on our liberties at home are deeply interconnected, and there is nothing antisemitic about recognizing that fact," it continued.

CNN STAFFERS SEE PARAMOUNT MERGER AS 'INEVITABLE' DESPITE LEGAL BATTLE DELAYING ELLISON TAKEOVER

Fonda knocked the proposed merger of Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros Discovery.

"They’re carrying so much debt. The Ellisons are carrying so much debt, and it’s being postponed now, so that they have to pay these huge sums. The merger would be terrible for consumers. Prices would go up. Thousands and thousands of people would lose their jobs, and as a creative, the fewer studios there are, the fewer places that we can take our products. We lose bargaining power. Unions lose their power," Fonda said. "There’s a very robust and growing movement to stop the mergers. It’s sad for me because I like David Ellison very much. David’s Skydance financed 'Grace and Frankie,' my 7-year-long run for Netflix. I got to know him, and I like him, but that doesn’t change things. This is not a personal thing."

Hollywood in Toto editor Christian Toto told Fox News Digital, "Jane Fonda isn't dumb. She uses some old-school misdirection to protect Mark Ruffalo from his own words. No one is arguing Ruffalo lacks a constitutional right to weigh in on the merger. What Ruffalo did with his comments is connect the merger to Israel's foreign policy."

"Ruffalo's bizarre attempt to make the deal about the Middle East, and blasting Israel as a genocidal state in the process, is what drew many people to the actor's comments. Fonda either is unaware of this or wants to fool anyone foolish enough to take her seriously," he continued.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Fonda also declared in the interview that she's not afraid of Trump.

"I’ve had my life. [President Donald] Trump can do nothing to me. I’m not scared, but that’s not true for everyone," she said. "More and more people are speaking out because their whole lives are at risk right now. AI could take everything away, and then data centers are being put in their neighborhoods, so there’s been a shift in the U.S. Things are changing. Republicans and Democrats alike are saying, ‘No, you’re not going to put a data center in my community.’ We can see now that even MAGA members are not liking the fact that their leaders are profiting off misery and cruelty. They don’t like the chaos that’s happening."

item.title: First responders honor World Trade Center beam arriving at Boston fallen heroes memorial
item.description: The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America tour brought a 21-foot World Trade Center beam to the Massachusetts Fallen Heroes Memorial in Boston.
item.content:encoded:
The Tunnel to Towers Steel Across America tour honored fallen heroes in Boston Wednesday as part of a nationwide tour slated to finish in New York City just after Sept. 11.

The group brought a preserved 21-foot steel beam from the South Tower of the World Trade Center, which has been on tour since May, to the Massachusetts Fallen Heroes Memorial in Boston's Seaport.

"For us as first responders and veterans, what this means as we come up on the 25th anniversary is personal. It's all about educating the next generation and not forgetting the sacrifices, not only made on 9/11 but what we've endured in the 20 years after in all theaters of combat," said Dan Magoon, executive director of Massachusetts Fallen Heroes.

AMERICA’S HEARTLAND COMES FACE-TO-FACE WITH 9/11 HISTORY AS 25TH ANNIVERSARY NEARS

Mike Eruzione, captain of the 1980 U.S. Winter Olympics hockey team that won the historic "Miracle on Ice" game against the Soviet Union, honored his friends who were passengers on one of the hijacked planes involved in the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

"It touched the heart of our country. It touched the souls of our country," Eruzione said of Tunnel to Towers, which helps 9/11 families, first responders and veterans rebuild in part from funds raised through nationwide charity runs.

FRANK SILLER: 'I LOVE YOU, BROTHER' — THE 9/11 LOSS THAT INSPIRED A MISSION OF SERVICE

The gathering brought together first responders from Massachusetts as well as law enforcement. Guests were allowed to approach the 16,900-pound beam and pay their respects.

"It's just crazy to think about where it once stood, the people that worked inside the buildings, the people that rushed inside to save those people and what happened when it all came down," said Daniel McCarthy, a Bostonian whose parents are from New York.

WHERE TUNNEL TO TOWERS' STEEL ACROSS AMERICA TOUR WILL STOP AHEAD OF 9/11

The beam was brought to Fenway Park Wednesday night after traveling to the U.S. Military Academy at West Point Monday.

On Sept. 8, the tour will stop at the White House in Washington, D.C.

item.title: Sean McVay expects every Rams player to be on flight to Australia for Week 1, including Aaron Donald
item.description: Sean McVay says he expects Aaron Donald, and every other Rams player, to be on the flight to Australia for Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams won’t be arriving in Australia with the San Francisco 49ers this week, instead opting to leave Wednesday and arriving the day before kickoff.

But that’s not the biggest piece of news regarding the NFL’s first-ever game in Australia — it’s who head coach Sean McVay expects to be on the flight with him down under.

McVay told reporters on Friday that he expects every player to make the trip to Australia, including Aaron Donald, the three-time Defensive Player of the Year who came out of retirement to join what has become a Rams superteam for the 2026 season.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Since he declared he would come out of retirement, Donald’s Week 1 status was always in the air. He didn’t get the same training camp the rest of the team had, though he is still in tremendous football shape. McVay even noted that he’s still not sure what will happen with Donald against their NFC West foe in Week 1.

But the fact Donald will be on the plane means he has a chance to play straight away for Los Angeles. In fact, McVay playing coy could just be gamesmanship for his respected colleague and fellow head coach, Kyle Shanahan.

'WE BACK': AARON DONALD RETURNS TO THE RAMS AND A DEFENSE NOW LOADED WITH MYLES GARRETT AND OTHERS

Instead, McVay said that the team is taking things "one day at a time" with the eight-time All-Pro defensive tackle who will end up in Canton one day. So, even though he should be on the flight, Rams fans should make sure "cautious" is in front of "optimism" when discussing Donald’s Week 1 status.

It’s hard for them, and football fans in general, not to be excited about No. 99 returning to the Rams this season. He spent 10 years in the NFL, earning Pro Bowl honors and creating nightmares for every offensive line and quarterback he faced.

If that wasn’t enough, Donald will be next to Myles Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year and a game-wrecker in his own right, on a defensive line made straight out of a video game.

While Rams fans await the return of Donald for real on the gridiron, they’re also looking to see if top wide receiver Puka Nacua will be suiting up against the 49ers as well. McVay gave an update during Friday’s presser, saying he is "making good progress" as he’s dealt with a psoas injury (core muscle connecting the lower spine and pelvis to thigh bones).

"Been hitting some high-speed yards at a really good clip with [Rams sports medicine and performance senior vice president] Reggie [Scott] and his group. And when we get back out there, it’ll be fun to have him," McVay said, per ESPN.

The NFL is also still reviewing Nacua under its personal conduct policy regarding an off-the-field lawsuit filed against him. However, he wasn’t placed on the commissioner’s exempt list, meaning he would avoid a suspension at least at the start of the season.

GEORGE KITTLE, NICK BOSA MAKE THE FLIGHT AS 49ERS HEAD TO AUSTRALIA FOR HISTORIC OPENER: REPORTS

A woman sued Nacua in March, claiming he made an antisemitic remark during a New Year’s Eve interaction and allegedly bit her shoulder and her friend’s thumb. Nacua’s lawyer, Levi McCarthern, denied that his client made an antisemitic remark.

So, while it is still possible that Nacua doesn’t play Week 1 due to potential discipline from the league, McVay saying he expects everyone to make the flight is once again a good sign for Nacua.

The 49ers are also benefitting from players being on the plane, as tight end George Kittle and defensive end Nick Bosa, both recovering from season-ending injuries last year, made the trip to Melbourne.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy mistrial declared after jury deadlocks in killings of her three children
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's trial centered on whether severe mental illness relieved her of criminal responsibility in the January 2023 deaths of her three children.
item.content:encoded:
Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Friday in Lindsay Clancy’s murder case after jurors said they were unable to reach a unanimous verdict in the killings of her three children after a week of deliberating at the Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Massachusetts.

The mistrial followed a dramatic dispute over an alleged 11-1 divide, with Clancy’s defense arguing that the lone holdout juror had acknowledged doubt but was refusing to properly apply the court’s instructions on reasonable doubt.

The alleged holdout is believed to be one of the three male jurors on the 12-person panel after defense attorney Kevin Reddington repeatedly referred to the unnamed juror as a male inside and outside court.

POSTPARTUM MOM LINDSAY CLANCY ON TRIAL FOR MURDER BRINGS COURT TO A HALT WITH SUDDEN BREAKDOWN

"[The other jurors] know that they were robbed — by one man — for whatever his agenda was, who stole seven weeks of the life of these other jurors that were so attentive, so beautiful, so wonderful and listened to this evidence," he told reporters after leaving the courthouse. 

"And you could see how defeated they were sitting there. And I got a funny feeling they could go one for another week if they had to. So, I hope that guy can sleep well at night." 

Also speaking outside the courthouse, Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz acknowledged the victims in this case — the Clancy children: 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan. 

"It is our job to make sure the victims are not invisible," Cruz said. "I am a father and a grandfather, and I cannot imagine the hell this entire family has lived through."

Clancy’s attorneys made an emergency appeal to the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court in an attempt to stay the mistrial and force further inquiry into the juror. Justice Dalila Argaez Wendlandt denied the request Friday afternoon, clearing the way for Sullivan to formally declare the mistrial.

HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL

Clancy had been charged with first-degree murder in the January 2023 deaths of her children, each of whom had been strangled with exercise bands.

The trial centered on whether she was legally responsible for her actions at the time, and the defense argued she wasn't due to postpartum psychosis.

Her attorneys argued that severe mental illness left her unable to appreciate the wrongfulness of what she was doing or unable to conform her conduct to the requirements of the law.

LINDSAY CLANCY’S HUSBAND COULD TESTIFY FOR HER AT TRIAL OVER DEATHS OF THEIR THREE CHILDREN

Prosecutors maintained that Clancy remained criminally responsible and pointed to evidence they said showed planning, purposeful behavior and an awareness of what she was doing before, during and after the killings.

During the trial, Clancy's former husband, Patrick Clancy, testified about the day of the slayings, which happened while he was running errands that included picking up children's stool softener at a CVS store and takeout for dinner. They spoke on the phone while he was out.

Under Massachusetts law, once lack of criminal responsibility is properly raised, prosecutors must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that a defendant was criminally responsible.

The mistrial means the case ended without a verdict, and Clancy was neither convicted nor acquitted. Prosecutors can seek to retry her but have not yet announced a decision.

LOUDOUN COUNTY HIGH SCHOOL STUDENT ACCUSED OF FILMING STUDENTS IN BATHROOM UNDER INVESTIGATION

FLORIDA MAN ALLEGEDLY RECORDED GIRLS IN CHURCH BATHROOM WITH HIDDEN CAMERA, ARRESTED ON VOYEURISM CHARGES

MICHIGAN DEMOCRAT DEMANDS REPORTERS STOP ASKING 'ABOUT HASAN PIKER' AHEAD OF SENATE RACE

DEM CANDIDATE ERUPTS IN PROFANE DEFENSE OF HASAN PIKER AS PARTY FIGURES DISTANCE THEMSELVES

item.title: Americans headed for high-risk nation urged to prepare wills, leave DNA samples ahead of time

item.content:encoded:
Americans who may be planning a trip to Libya are being urged to reconsider those plans, as the U.S. State Department has issued its strongest possible travel warning.

The department recently updated Libya's Level 4 "Do Not Travel" advisory, warning Americans not to visit the country for any reason due to crime, terrorism, health concerns, unrest, kidnapping and landmines. The overall advisory level did not change.

"Do not travel to Libya for any reason," the advisory states.

The State Department warns that clashes between armed groups and government-aligned forces can break out at any time — while weapons are widespread throughout the country.

Criminal organizations are known to be involved in drug and human trafficking and other smuggling activity, while targeted kidnappings and assassinations are common, according to the advisory.

"Kidnapping is widespread, and victims have included U.S. citizens," officials warn.

Americans could also have limited options for help in an emergency.

"There is currently no U.S. Embassy in Libya," the advisory states. 

It added that the U.S. government cannot provide emergency services to Americans in the country because of the security risks.

The State Department also warns that terrorist attacks could occur with little or no warning, while demonstrations can turn violent and disrupt transportation and other essential services.

Landmines and unexploded ordnance pose another danger throughout the North African country, with officials warning that their locations are often unmarked or difficult to recognize.

Travelers are advised to avoid roadside ditches, shoulders and unmarked trails and never touch anything that could be unexploded munitions.

For Americans who decide to travel to Libya despite the warning, the State Department recommends having a plan to leave in an emergency that does not depend on U.S. government assistance.

The State Department further recommends establishing a "proof of life protocol" with loved ones in case a traveler is taken hostage.

"Leave DNA samples with your medical provider in case it is necessary for your family to access them for identification purposes," the advisory states.

The warning comes as U.S. officials continue issuing travel and security advisories for destinations around the world.

item.title: Scientists discover new tick-borne virus after testing thousands of patients with mysterious illnesses
item.description: The Asian longhorned tick nairovirus caused flu-like illness and thrombocytopenia in over 10% of tick-bitten patients studied in a China lab.
item.content:encoded:
Scientists in China have identified a previously unknown tick-borne virus that can cause flu-like illness, fatigue and gastrointestinal symptoms, according to a new study.

The newly discovered virus, the Asian longhorned tick nairovirus (ALTNV), which is part of the orthonairovirus group, has also been found to cause thrombocytopenia (reduced blood platelet counts) and laboratory evidence of liver-cell injury or inflammation.

Since 2009, Chinese researchers have been tracking patients with unusual illnesses, including severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), according to Dr. Sharon Nachman, chief of pediatric infectious diseases at Stony Brook Children’s Hospital in New York.

NO CURE, NO VACCINE: EXPERTS WARN OF RARE BOURBON VIRUS AFTER FIRST NY CASE

"Thrombocytopenia is low platelet count, so those patients bled, and it had about a 30% mortality, which is quite high," she told Fox News Digital. "So, they kept following those patients."

Many of the cases were linked to Dabie bandavirus (DBV), a tick-borne hemorrhagic fever, but it was not the most common virus.

After extensive testing of blood samples and viral fragments, researchers identified the new virus, ALTNV, which is genetically distinct from DBV.

Researchers from the State Key Laboratory of Pathogen and Biosecurity in Beijing identified the virus in 10.4% of 3,163 patients who had been bitten by ticks.

HANTAVIRUS IN THE US: WHERE THE RARE, SOMETIMES DEADLY DISEASE HAS BEEN FOUND

Patients who had both ALTNV and DBV were more likely to have respiratory issues and kidney complications. Seven (18.4%) of these patients died during the course of the study.

"The cocirculation of ALTNV and DBV in the same areas, coupled with their shared tick vector, underscores the need for improved differential diagnosis between infections with these viruses in regions where SFTS is endemic," the authors concluded.

The findings were published this week in the New England Journal of Medicine.

"The big picture is that ticks carry lots of viruses," Nachman said. "We're getting smarter at identifying those viruses. And when one blood sample is negative, it's important to say, 'Maybe there was a new virus there, and let's look for it.'"

Illness from ALTNV can initially resemble the flu, causing fever, muscle aches, fatigue and sometimes respiratory symptoms.

Although an ALTNV infection can cause low platelet counts, the study did not link the virus alone to severe bleeding or deaths. The fatal cases involved patients who were also infected with DBV, which causes severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome.

Because tick-borne viral symptoms can overlap with many infections, Nachman emphasized the importance of identifying the specific virus.

"Effective antivirals exist for flu, but not for many tick-borne viruses, including the newly identified one," she said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

For most patients, supportive care is given to help manage symptoms, "but it's also about being smart and not giving patients the wrong medication," Nachman noted. "And we certainly don't want to use antibiotics because those only work for bacteria, not for viruses."

Nachman shared the best practices she recommends to families looking to avoid tick bites.

"Wear the right clothing, meaning long pants, tucking them into your socks, and use tick repellents on your skin if you're an adult or on your clothing if you're a young child," she advised.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

It’s also important to be on the lookout for ticks on the skin.

"The longer the tick is on your skin, the more it's engorged, the more it’s likely to pass an infection to you," Nachman said. "So, removing them after you've gone hiking or walking on the beach will be really important."

While the Asian longhorn tick is not yet seen in the U.S., Nachman noted there are "lots and lots of other ticks, and those ticks carry other diseases."

"I don't want to say one tick is worse than another tick. It's rather all about the diseases they carry and who you are," she said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"So, if you're a healthy adult, and you get babesiosis, you often get better without any medications. But if you're an immune-compromised adult, you're going to be quite sick.

"It’s not really about the ticks. It’s about the patient. Who are you? What's your underlying illness if you have any? How old are you, and how healthy are you?"

item.title: Non-citizen police officers approved after Dem says ICE 'invasion' 'sends a message'
item.description: Danbury, Connecticut's city council voted 18-2 to let non-citizen immigrants and DACA recipients serve as police officers amid ongoing ICE raids.
item.content:encoded:
After a week of ICE raids, the Democrat-dominated City Council of Danbury, Connecticut, voted nearly unanimously to approve non-citizen legal residents serving as police officers.

Under the new guidance, approved in an 18-2 vote, non-citizen legal residents and Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) recipients living in Danbury are allowed to serve as police officers in Danbury.

"There is no reason to vote against this, and if you do vote against this, I truly question your moral compass," he added.

Britton told Fox News Digital that "Danbury is an immigrant city, and I believe someone who is lawfully here, committed to our community, and willing to raise their hand and take an oath to protect and serve should have the opportunity to do so."

He added that "this change does not lower Danbury’s standards for becoming a police officer. It simply allows otherwise qualified lawful permanent residents and DACA recipients to apply and compete for these positions."

He noted that "every applicant must still satisfy the same training, background, character, and certification requirements required of any other officer," saying, "This was about expanding the pool of qualified applicants while maintaining the same high standards our residents expect from their police department."

Similarly, Taylor O'Brien, a spokesperson for the Danbury city government, told Fox News Digital that council "amended its ordinance in accordance with Connecticut's Police Officer Standards and Training Council, allowing legal permanent residents and DACA recipients to apply to become officers in the Danbury Police Department."

DEM SENATE NOMINEE CHANGES TUNE ON ICE AFTER VOWING NOT 'ONE MORE DIME' FOR AGENCY

O'Brien said that "this standard is followed by over 30 municipalities in Connecticut and several states across the country" and that it "opens Danbury's applicant pool to otherwise qualified candidates, including legal Danbury residents, who are currently applying to be police officers in other communities."

In 2020, the Connecticut Police Officer Standards and Training Council "partially waived" the citizenship requirement, extending eligibility for law enforcement candidates in Connecticut to lawful permanent residents and DACA recipients, according to the Connecticut Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection.

O'Brien added that Danbury Mayor Roberto Alves, a Democrat, "ensures Danbury maintains a rigorous hiring process for our Police Officers," adding that "this amendment should encourage qualified residents from the Danbury community to apply to serve the City they call home."

According to the Danbury News Times, Alves himself immigrated to the U.S. as an "undocumented child" and gained citizenship in 2017.

The outlet quoted Alves saying he is "glad the City Council approved" the measure.
